description: Record ADR 0048: the cam-spec operator-interactive grill stays in the orchestrator context (orch/worker boundary is LLM-non-interactive, not all-LLM).

userStories.title: Write ADR 0048: grill stays in orchestrator context
userStories.description: As the cam-cli maintainer, I need an Architectural Decision Record capturing the CAM-197 grill decision (the cam-spec operator-interactive grill stays in the orchestrator context and does not move to a dedicated pane) so that the orch/worker boundary rationale is durable and the whole CAM-197 epic is framed by a recorded, gate-passing decision.
acceptanceCriteria: A new ADR file docs/adr/0048-cam-spec-grill-stays-in-orchestrator-context.md exists and records that the cam-spec grill stays in the orchestrator context rather than moving to a dedicated pane. [oracle: grep -q 'grill stays in the orchestrator context' docs/adr/0048-cam-spec-grill-stays-in-orchestrator-context.md]

The ADR records that the orchestrator/worker boundary is drawn at LLM-non-interactive work, not all LLM work. [oracle: grep -q 'LLM-non-interactive' docs/adr/0048-cam-spec-grill-stays-in-orchestrator-context.md]

The ADR follows the existing ADR structure (top-level '# ADR 0048:' title plus '## Context', '## Decision', '## Consequences' sections) consistent with 0047. [oracle: grep -q '^# ADR 0048:' docs/adr/0048-cam-spec-grill-stays-in-orchestrator-context.md]

The ADR explicitly addresses all three ADR admission gates (hard-to-reverse: redefines the epic boundary; surprising-without-context: contradicts the literal 'orch only converses' reading; genuine trade-off: single human-facing interface vs orchestrator context preservation) as the justification for recording it. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The ADR captures the token-cost rationale: the ~50k-token grill cost is shed by the cycle-close recycle (zero post-spec value) and belongs to a single PR cycle, so it does not violate the one-PR-per-session invariant. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
Any src path referenced in the ADR actually exists on disk (doc-as-code gate ADR-0037 allowlist); reference only real paths or phrase to avoid unverifiable path claims. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

The ADR is a human-readable .md following the operator no-em-dash convention (colons, parentheses, periods only). [oracle: ! grep -q '\xe2\x80\x94' docs/adr/0048-cam-spec-grill-stays-in-orchestrator-context.md]
No code, config, or command behavior changed: the only added/modified file is the new ADR. [oracle: file-assert git diff --name-only main includes only docs/adr/0048-*.md]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
The full quality spine remains green with the ADR added. [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: DOC-ONLY: create docs/adr/0048-cam-spec-grill-stays-in-orchestrator-context.md, no code/config/command edits. Next ADR number is 0048 (0047-backendadapter-seam is latest on main); do not collide. Mirror the section structure of docs/adr/0047-*.md (# ADR NNNN: title / ## Context / ## Decision / ## Consequences). Comparands 'grill stays in the orchestrator context' and 'LLM-non-interactive' must appear verbatim. Be consistent with prior ADRs 0020 (orchestrator runs as an enforced agent), 0028 (orchestrator context window is configured), 0029 (context backstop must produce a handoff before arming). doc-as-code gate (ADR-0037) verifies any referenced src path exists on disk: reference only real paths (e.g. src/supervisor/review.ts, .claude/skills/grilling, the cam-spec command) or phrase to avoid path claims. Follow the persisted-doc no-em-dash convention (global CLAUDE.md). Grep scripts/cam/patterns.md for 'ADR' / 'doc-as-code' before writing.
